sites.name: Theodore Roosevelt National Park
sites.tr: T.R. came to the Dakota Badlands in 1883 to hunt bison and stayed to run the Maltese Cross and Elkhorn ranches. The park protects the country where he ranched.

sites.name: Sagamore Hill National Historic Site
sites.tr: T.R.'s home from 1885 until his death in 1919, and the Summer White House during his presidency.

sites.name: Theodore Roosevelt Birthplace National Historic Site
sites.tr: A reconstruction of the brownstone at 28 East 20th Street where T.R. was born on October 27, 1858.

sites.name: Theodore Roosevelt Inaugural National Historic Site
sites.tr: In the Ansley Wilcox House, T.R. took the oath of office on September 14, 1901, after the death of President William McKinley.

sites.name: Yellowstone National Park
sites.tr: T.R. toured Yellowstone in April 1903 and laid the cornerstone of the North Entrance arch that now carries his name.

sites.name: Devils Tower National Monument
sites.tr: On September 24, 1906, T.R. proclaimed Devils Tower the first national monument under the Antiquities Act.

sites.name: Mesa Verde National Park
sites.tr: T.R. signed the act creating Mesa Verde National Park on June 29, 1906. The park protects thousands of archaeological sites, including cliff dwellings built by Ancestral Pueblo people.

sites.name: Wind Cave National Park
sites.tr: On January 9, 1903, T.R. signed the bill making Wind Cave a national park.

sites.name: Grand Canyon National Park
sites.tr: T.R. visited the South Rim in May 1903 and proclaimed Grand Canyon National Monument on January 11, 1908.

sites.name: Petrified Forest National Park
sites.tr: T.R. proclaimed Petrified Forest National Monument on December 8, 1906.

sites.name: Muir Woods National Monument
sites.tr: T.R. proclaimed Muir Woods National Monument on January 9, 1908, on redwood land donated by William and Elizabeth Kent.

sites.name: Crater Lake National Park
sites.tr: Crater Lake became a national park on May 22, 1902, when T.R. signed the bill creating it.
